_meta.role: Embedded Software Engineer II, Ring Firmware

summary: Recent M.S. Computer Engineering graduate from Rochester Institute of Technology (RIT), NY with embedded firmware experience in C/C++ on ARM Cortex-M4 (STM32) microcontrollers. Wrote bare-metal drivers and interrupt service routines for ADC, I2C, UART and PWM, and ran FreeRTOS tasks on real hardware. Debugged hardware-software boundaries with logic analyzers and oscilloscopes, and integrated Bluetooth links and Python tooling in a wearable device.

experience.title: Embedded Systems Intern
bullets: Developed a wearable gesture-recognition glove for hands-free cursor control integrating ADXL345 accelerometers with Raspberry Pi and HC-05 Bluetooth to translate 3-DoF hand motion into HID commands via Python.
Implemented a custom tap-detection algorithm using z-axis differential thresholding; resolved sensor jitter through software calibration and resolution tuning.

experience.title: Python Developer Intern
bullets: Used GitLab for version control and JupyterHub for collaborative data analysis and technical documentation.
Developed a Python GUI using PyQt and Matplotlib for real-time data acquisition and experimental visualization in a laboratory environment.

projects.name: STM32 Bare-Metal Temperature Monitor
bullets: Programmed peripherals directly in bare-metal C on a Cortex-M4 (GPIO, TIM2, ADC1, I2C1); achieved 3.68 KB Flash / 1.58 KB RAM at a deterministic 1 Hz update rate; verified in Proteus.
Implemented timer-triggered ADC scan conversions, interrupt-driven sample capture (interrupt service routines), and a low-level I2C driver.

projects.name: Object Tracking Turret
bullets: Implemented multi-servo PWM control with interrupt-driven UART commands and user override on STM32, with YOLOv8 on NVIDIA Jetson sending control commands over UART.
Used FreeRTOS with mutexes for shared-memory task coordination; integrated VL53L0X ToF sensing and OLED distance visualization.

projects.name: Robocon Competition Robot — Holonomic Drive & Encoder Odometry
bullets: Implemented interrupt-driven quadrature decoding from first principles, a 4-bit A/B transition state machine on hardware interrupts, and drove four motor channels at 15 kHz PWM on Arduino Due.

projects.name: Voice-Controlled Robotic Arm (COFFIN) — MS Capstone, RIT
bullets: Built a voice-controlled pick-and-place system with a Jetson+Arduino controller; used dual VL53L0X ToF sensors via a TCA9548A I2C mux for gripper-triggered close at 25 mm, achieving 100% pick reliability (10/10 trials).
